segmenti.tekst: نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره

ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، أرسله الله بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وسراجا منيرا، لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين، صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين وسلم تسليما كثيرا إلى يوم الدين.

قال الله في كتابه الكريم: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون. أما بعد. Praise belongs to the One, Exalted Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), Lord of all the worlds, Lord of the Day of Judgment, Lord of jinn and mankind, and blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.
Dear brothers, respected congregation, when we talk about islah, or reforming the general condition in the community, we are talking about a great goal.
We are talking about a great goal and the mission of all the prophets. The prophets, dear brothers, were not sent by Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, only to deliver the revelation to us,
but also to reform, to reform the condition. When Shu'ayb, alayhis-salatu was-salam, advised his people not to cheat on the scales, the steelyard, the liter measure, they accused him of lying.

What was his answer to that? Shu'ayb, alayhis-salatu was-salam, said: “In uridu illa al-islaha mastata'tu.” He said: “I want only to reform as much as I am able,” as much as is within my ability. And he said: “My success is with Allah.” And my success is with Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. And all of us, dear brothers, should strive, like Shu'ayb, to reform the condition

as much as we are able. And all of us are able to some extent. But sometimes a person hurries, and instead of reforming his own condition, his personal condition, he sets out to reform the condition in the neighborhood, in the community, while neglecting himself. A person should first start with himself.
He should ask himself: what is my condition, my relationship with my Lord? What is my relationship with my Lord? Do I know my Lord? Do I know the One whom I worship?

What is my relationship with prayer? Do I pray all five daily prayers? Do I fall in prostration before my Lord? What is my relationship with His revelation, the Qur'an? Have I learned the letters, do I know how to recite the Qur'an? Do I at least understand something of that Qur'an? What is my relationship with my family, with my parents, with my wife, with my children?

Well, when a person reforms that, then he can reform the condition in the neighborhood, in the community, and so on, and so forth. Also, for a person to set out to reform the condition of a community, he needs to have knowledge for it.

He needs to have knowledge for it. Not everyone can reform the condition in the community. A person needs to have knowledge for it, to read the sirah (biography) of the prophets, especially the sirah of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

You know what the Arabs were before the Prophet, and what the Arabs were after the Prophet. We are not talking about those Arabs, that is, about today's Arabs, but about the Arabs of that time who came to rule the world after the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Before the Prophet they were ordinary Bedouins: no state, nothing, no laws.

After the Prophet – the peak of civilization, of science. That is why a person… and the prophets are our most beautiful example. When a person reads the sirah of the prophets, especially the sirah of our Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, then he will know how he will reform the condition and will be able to reform it.
Unfortunately, we are a somewhat strange people, and when someone sets out to reform the condition in the community, when the people begin to protest, when the people begin to awaken, what happens?

We come to the point where there are people who only criticize. You know, they are good with words, but he won't reform the condition, nothing suits him, only criticism. If you ask him about the air pollution in our city, he will say: “Oh, it's a catastrophe.” Go out and ask, everyone will say: it's a catastrophe.
But when winter comes, dear brothers, what do we do? To save a few cubic meters of firewood, we burn tires, plastic, and so on, and so forth. We ourselves are to blame that the air is like that.
If you ask people on the street what the situation is regarding the cleanliness of the city, hygiene, everyone will say: “Oh, it's no good at all.”

But when it comes to picking up that garbage, not throwing garbage, teaching our children not to throw that garbage, we are nowhere to be found. Who throws that garbage if not us? People don't come from Leskovac to throw garbage on us.

Rather, we throw that garbage and then we complain that the city is in a catastrophic state. Instead of our children… as I said, we should start with ourselves, first examine ourselves: that is not right. Then our children, then our neighbors. And when we see someone throw something, to pick it up, to give it back, to give that garbage back, and so on, and so on.

And that is how the condition is reformed, that is how, that is how [unclear] the condition is reformed. That is, we start with ourselves, then our families, and so on, and so forth. But how can a person reform the condition in the most beautiful way? The way the Qur'an teaches us.

That we set things right, that is, that we reconcile our brothers. That, if we see that someone has fallen out with someone, that they have bad relations, a person makes peace. That a person makes peace. And that is what the Qur'an advises us.

That is what the Qur'an tells us. It says: make peace, make peace between your brothers. And when the Muslims understand one another, when we here understand one another, then our condition will be, will be, will be better. But look, dear brothers, not everyone, not every reform, not every reform is islah, true reform of the condition. Already in the time of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, there were those hypocrites
who said… “وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ” [unclear – translation of the verse] “قَالُوا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ” [unclear] who establish order.

That is what the hypocrites said in the time of the Prophet Muhammad, and to this very day we have those who speak like that. And you will see a prime minister of Israel come out and say: “We are establishing order in Gaza.

We are not causing disorder.” That is what the Qur'an tells us. But in fact they are causing the greatest disorder on this Earth. But with the emergence of these social networks, the media, this information is simply put out and people easily believe it.

And then we come to the point that they are supposedly really reforming the situation. But this is not the situation only in Palestine, it is the situation in the whole world. As there, so here among us. So you will see corruption, bribery, party-based employment, family-based employment, the employment of loyal subjects.

And then when you tell people: “People, this is not right, let's change something” – “No,” they say, “it's all good, it's all fine.” For the sake of – wait – for the sake of personal, personal interests. And believe me, dear brothers, the greatest fasad (corruption), the greatest fasad and the greatest [unclear]

is when the political and religious elites join together and then support one another. And we have such examples everywhere in the world, in the Arab world. And then we have the political elite that does all sorts of things, and we have the religious elite that justifies it with proofs from the Qur'an and hadith.

But as in the world, so here among us. And that is the greatest fasad: that we have a political elite telling people how everything is fine, how everything is great, and then we have that religious elite that supports it, that supports the same thing, unfortunately.

So, a person, as we said, should begin as far as is within his ability. That is, he should start with himself, and when he has reformed himself, reform his wife, his family, and after that set out to reform his neighbor, and so on, and so forth, and our condition will be better.

And that is how the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam… Someone will say: “That's all well, efendi, but it's very hard.” How so? In the time of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, it was much harder still. Much harder still. Incomparably harder.

And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, slowly, over 23 years, slowly began with his own family. The first to accept Islam were his wife, Khadijah, and so on, and so on, and so on. That is, until the whole, the whole community was reformed.

I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among those who reform the condition of their community, and not among those who destroy it. I ask Him, the Exalted, to forgive us our sins and the sins of our parents, and to admit us into Jannah (Paradise). Amin, ya Rabb al-alamin. Barakallahu li wa lakum fil-Qur'an al-'azim, wa nafa'ani wa iyyakum bima fihi min al-ayati wadh-dhikr al-hakim. Aqulu qawli hadha wa astaghfirullaha li wa lakum, fastaghfiruhu, innahu huwa al-Ghafur ar-Rahim.
